newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA CALL MONEY HIGHER, CENTRAL BANK UPS RATES.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA CALL MONEY HIGHER, CENTRAL BANK UPS RATES.

text.p: Jakarta call money rose to 23.0 percent from 17.0 percent on Wednesday morning, dealers said.
They said demand was brisk, pushing overnight money to 19.0 percent level in mid-morning before a central bank interest rates hike sent overall rates higher.
The bank raised interest rates for central bank certificates (SBIs) of all maturities by 100 basis points.

The central bank raised its overnight bilateral central bank certificate rates to 15.0 percent from 14.0 percent, two-to-six day SBIs to 16.0 percent from 15.0 percent, one-week to 10.5 from 9.5, two-week to 11.0 from 10.0, one-month to 11.625 from 10.625, three to 11.5 from 10.5, six to 12.125 from 11.125 and one-year to 12.75 from 11.75 percent.
The central bank also remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market.
The central bank cut its bilateral SBI rates for papers above one-week by 50 basis points last Friday after the foreign exchange market showed signs of stabilisation.
However, renewed pressure spilling over from neighbouring countries knocked the rupiah down further, forcing the central bank to impose a tighter money policy to contain speculation.
Dealers said longer-term rates were higher after the rates hike, with one-week money rising to 17.0/17.5 percent and one-month money to 18.0/18.5 percent.
But one local bank dealer said the higher longer-term rates should not affect the market significantly because interbank rates were already higher than bilateral rates.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 18.97 percent, compared with 15.62 percent on Monday.
